title: Impact of M&A Announcements on Stock Returns

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy

We will use an Event Study approach to analyze the impact of M&A announcements on stock returns. This method is suitable because it allows us to measure the abnormal returns around the event window, which in this case is the M&A announcement. The key assumption is that the stock returns are not systematically different from the market returns in the absence of the event. We will estimate the cumulative abnormal returns (CAR) around the event day and test whether they are significantly different from zero.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required libraries
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Read the data
data <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s52_data.csv")

# Calculate abnormal returns
data <- data %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  mutate(ret_adj = ret - beta * (mkt_ret - mean(mkt_ret)))

# Define the event window
data <- data %>%
  mutate(event_window = event_day)

# Calculate cumulative abnormal returns (CAR)
car <- data %>%
  filter(event_window >= -10 & event_window <= 10) %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  summarise(car = sum(ret_adj), .groups = 'drop')

# Print the CAR
print(car)

# Basic robustness check: Check if CAR is significantly different from zero
t_test <- t.test(car$car)
print(t_test)
```

## 3. Expected Findings

We expect the cumulative abnormal returns (CAR) to be positive around the event day (M&A announcement). This is because M&A announcements are generally associated with positive news, which can lead to an increase in stock prices. The magnitude of the CAR will depend on the specific M&A deals and the market's perception of their potential impact. However, we expect the CAR to be significantly different from zero, indicating that the M&A announcements have a statistically significant impact on stock returns.

_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The merger announcement leads to a positive abnormal return.
